Priya Shah: Hey team, first week checklist item: I installed Okta Gateway and cant reach internal name `bastion.corp.redwood` from my WSL shell. Windows says connected, but `ssh bastion.corp.redwood` times out. Anyone hit this on WSL2 + Windows 11?
Javier Morales: welcome Priya! quick Qs: is the Okta client the browser-based Gateway or the native agent? also can you paste `wsl -l -v` and `ipconfig /all` (redact macs/serials) or `route print`?
Priya Shah: using Okta Gateway via browser + local agent. wsl -l -v shows my ubuntu-22.04 running. route print shows corporate CIDR 10.2.0.0 via 172.31.254.1 on interface 25, but from WSL `ip route` shows default via 172.28.48.1 and no 10.2.0.0 route. nslookup bastion.corp.redwood returns no answer from WSL.
Sam W.: known WSL quirk: WSL has its own networking namespace and sometimes doesn't inherit Windows VPN routes/DNS. Two quick workarounds: 1) add a Windows host entry for the bastion private IP (`C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts`) so WSL resolves and you can `ssh user@10.2.12.3`, or 2) add the route inside WSL: `sudo ip route add 10.2.0.0/16 via 172.28.48.1` (replace gw with `ip route | grep default` gw).
Priya Shah: I tried adding hosts on Windows but WSL still couldn't ping the IP. When I `curl ifconfig.me` inside WSL I see my corp IP (so traffic goes out) but traceroute to 10.2.12.3 drops at the WSL gateway.
Javier Morales: hm. Another thing: Okta Gateway can push internal DNS via the Windows resolver, but WSL won't use Windows DNS by default. You can enable Windows DNS resolution in WSL by adding `nameserver 172.28.48.1` to `/etc/resolv.conf` (but note WSL regenerates that on restart). For a persistent approach: create `/etc/wsl.conf` with `[network] generateResolvConf = false`, then write resolv.conf manually. Quick, non-persistent test: `echo 'nameserver 172.28.48.1' | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf && sudo chattr +i /etc/resolv.conf`
Priya Shah: I tried `sudo ip route add 10.2.0.0/16 via 172.28.48.1` and then `ssh ec2-user@10.2.12.3` and it connected! Why did the Windows route not show up in WSL though?
Sam W.: WSL2 uses a virtual NAT and doesn't automatically import all Windows routes. Okta-client pushes routes into Windows network stack; you still need to sync into WSL. The `wsl --shutdown` after changing hosts/resolv or adding routes sometimes helps if you modify Windows files that WSL mounts.
okta-bot: Okta Gateway session refreshed for Priya Shah. Browser MFA required to update pushed DNS/routes.
Priya Shah: re-authed Okta MFA just in case, then did `wsl --shutdown` and restarted WSL; my resolv.conf now has the corp DNS and I can resolve `bastion.corp.redwood` without a hosts hack.
infra-bot: Priya Shah's IAM tag `corp-ssh-access` status: pending. Infra reviewers: please approve to enable console SSM sessions.
Priya Shah: filed the infra request in #eng-infra with my employee ID. Thanks everyone 389
Javier Morales: summary for docs: WSL2 tip for new hires -> if internal hostnames or private CIDR unreachable after Okta Gateway, re-auth Okta, then either (1) add route inside WSL (`sudo ip route add 10.2.0.0/16 via <WSL_GW>`) or (2) persist Windows DNS into WSL by disabling auto-gen resolv.conf and writing corp DNS. We'll add this to the Windows onboarding checklist.
Priya Shah: saved, and added a note to my onboarding checklist: "If using WSL2, re-auth Okta + sync DNS/routes to WSL (or add temporary ip route)". All good now 389
